summary: Implemented AGENTSKILLS-IDE.md increment 1. Added YamlDotNet 18.1.0 (version verified live via api.nuget.org/v3-flatcontainer, usage verified via WebFetch of the real YamlDotNet README on raw.githubusercontent.com - not guessed from training data). Added src/ProjectName.ServiceDefaults/RepoPaths.cs (shared repo-root resolver, mirroring the existing AGENT_SKILLS_ROOT/PMCRO_ROOT env-var+walk-up pattern rather than a third duplicate). Added src/ProjectName.Api/Controllers/WorkspaceController.cs: GET api/workspace/index, reading agents.yaml, .agents/skills/*/SKILL.md frontmatter, mcp/ProjectName.Mcp.* (static list only, explicitly not claiming live tools/list discovery), .pmcro/trails + .pmcro/queue. Wired AppHost.cs (Workspace__RepoRoot for the API, WORKSPACE_API_URL for the JS app, same pattern as the existing AGUI_BACKEND_URL wiring). Added ui/.../app/api/workspace/route.ts server proxy and converted page.tsx's four inert nav buttons into working panels that fetch and render this data on click.
verification: dotnet build ProjectName.slnx: Build succeeded, 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s), all 7 projects

npm run lint (projectname-copilotkit): initially caught a real react-hooks/set-state-in-effect violation (setState called synchronously in a useEffect body) - fixed by moving the fetch into the nav button's click handler instead of an effect, since it is a response to a user action, not a render-synchronization concern. Second run: 0 problems.
npm run build (projectname-copilotkit): Compiled successfully, TypeScript check passed, /api/workspace listed as a route in the build output

Live smoke test: ran ProjectName.Api standalone (dotnet run, Workspace__RepoRoot set to the repo root) and curled GET /api/workspace/index directly - returned real parsed data: 24 agents from agents.yaml, 23 skills from .agents/skills (correctly showing null name/description for the one skill lacking YAML frontmatter), 3 MCP servers, governance counts matching the actual trail history (8 sealed/1 open/1 abandoned at the time), 2 example specs. This is genuine functional verification, not just a compile check.
not_covered: Did not run the full Aspire AppHost stack (Ollama + MCP servers + GrpcService + Api + the Next.js app together) - that requires GPU-backed Ollama and is out of scope/risk for this pass. The standalone Api smoke test above verifies the new endpoint's actual logic; it does not verify the browser-to-Next-proxy-to-Api round trip end-to-end in a running app.
